record.notes: 2026-10-23: the cloud plan has a public ingress with UDP. NetBird Reverse Proxy offers L4 'TCP', 'UDP' and 'TLS' service modes, and a UDP service is 'a UDP relay with session tracking. The proxy accepts UDP packets on the service's listen port and forwards them to your backend. Sessions are reaped after an idle timeout'. Cloud domains are free and appear 'with a Free badge'. The meter is discretionary: 'NetBird's cloud-hosted Reverse Proxy is provided on a shared, best-effort basis. High-volume or sustained data transfers may be subject to bandwidth limits, rate limiting, and fair-use policies', and 'These restrictions do not apply if you self-host NetBird'. Whether the Free plan is entitled to the feature is not stated on either the pricing page or the docs page.

record.notes: This is the only free-plan path found where a WireGuard peer gets a public TCP and UDP listener with no card and no account review, provided the feature is not gated. L4 services listen on a port on the proxy cluster and several services can share a port; custom ports depend on a cluster flag. A self-hosted deployment needs Traefik. The alternative reading, that Reverse Proxy is paid, cannot be excluded from the pages read, which is why the rung is unverified rather than documented. L4 services carry no browser SSO, only IP and country restrictions. Re-read 2026-10-23: the docs open with 'Availability: Reverse Proxy is currently in beta', and netbird expose needs an account administrator to enable Peer Expose and name allowed peer groups.
